chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Comping behind soloists: Art Tatum and Lester Young's drummer

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: See, trying to play too much and I've got to insert this while I'm playing that is one reason why Art Tatum wasn't a good big band pianist. Art could do it but Art felt as though he wasn't doing anything, playing with a big band, just comping. That's what's wrong with

a lot of drummers, they'll sit down, they don't think. They're putting a good support behind your solo in good rhythm, they think that they aren't doing anything and so they'll start doing their little thing behind your solo. Here's a funny story. Lester Young was going into the Birdland, so it was a time that I had a studio there in New York, Walter Thomas and I. This is before Gene Krupa. So Pres wanted a drummer and I had a very good drummer up there, at least he was good on the pad and could read, fast hands and everything, and I'd heard him play a couple of times around somewhere, I just can't pinpoint it now, he sounded good, but he needed that experience. And I said, Pres, I've got a boy up here, I said, but you've got to stay with him. I said he's got some nice hands and he will listen.
Was that Willy Jones by any chance?

No, No I know Willy Jones, no. I'm not going to call this boy's name. So anyway Pres says, okay, Cozy, and Pres did keep him, kept him there for his run at Birdland, but the first night, he went down there and this boy was up there, dropping bombs ... and Pres up there trying to take a solo you know, so Pres waited until the whole set was over and Pres went over to him and said, 'Pops,' he says, 'man, you're up there just playing your buns off. But behind my solos, just give me a little titty-boom, titty-boom, titty boom.' So the boy did that, you know, just give him a little
titly boom behind them solos. You know what I mean by titly boom (HUMMING).
